At-large | before_election = [[Peter Welch]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = TBD | after_party = TBD }} {{ElectionsVT}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Vermont]] from [[Vermont's at-large congressional district]]. The election coincided with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]]. The primaries will be held on August 14. [[Peter Welch]], a Democrat who was first elected in 2006, announced he would run for reelection to a seventh term. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Daniel Freilich, candidate for [[United States Senate election in Vermont, 2010|U.S. Senate in 2010]], Navy medical doctor, physician at the VA Medical Center * [[Peter Welch]], incumbent U.S. Representative ====Withdrawn==== * Ben Mitchell, [[Liberty Union Party|Liberty Union]] nominee for [[Governor of Vermont]] in [[Vermont gubernatorial election, 2010|2010]] and for [[Lieutenant Governor of Vermont]] in [[Vermont elections, 2012#Lieutenant Governor|2012]] ''(Withdrew 8/9/2018, endorsed Freilich)''{{cite web|url=https://vtdigger.org/2018/08/09/house-debate-mitchell-drops-backs-fellow-challenger |title=During House debate, Mitchell drops out and backs fellow challenger|accessdate=August 9, 2018|publisher=VTDigger}} ===Debates & forums=== * [https://www.cctv.org/watch-tv/programs/forum-democratic-primary-representative-congress CCTV Channel 17 Forum - Democratic Primary for Representative to Congress 8/7/2018] * [https://digital.vpr.net/post/campaign-2018-debate-democratic-candidates-us-house#stream/0 Vermont Public Radio - Campaign 2018: A Debate With The Democratic Candidates For U.S. House 8/9/2018] ===Results=== [[File:2018 VT-AL Democratic primary.svg|thumb|125px|Results by county: {{legend|#214478|Welch—80–90%}} {{legend|#2c5aa0|Welch—70–80%}} ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{cite web |website=https://vtelectionresults.sec.state.vt.us/Index.html#/federal |publisher=Secretary of State of Vermont |accessdate=15 August 2018}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Peter Welch]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 55,939 | percentage = 80.35% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Daniel Freilich | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 7,881 | percentage = 11.32% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Benjamin Mitchell | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 2,676 | percentage = 3.84% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Write-in | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 142 | percentage = 0.20% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Spoiled votes | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 52 | percentage = 0.08% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Blank votes | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 2,927 | percentage = 4.20% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 69,618 | percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box end}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * H. Brooke Paige, former CEO of Remmington News Service * Anya Tynio, sales representative for the [[Newport Daily Express]]{{cite web|url =https://digital.vpr.net/post/campaign-2018-gop-candidate-anya-tynio-running-us-house#stream/0 |title=GOP Candidate Anya Tynio running for U.S. House}} ===Debates & forums=== * [https://www.cctv.org/watch-tv/programs/republican-primary-forum-representative-congress CCTV Channel 17 Republican Primary Forum for Representative to Congress 7/23/2018] ===Results=== [[File:2018 VT-AL GOP primary.svg|thumb|125px|Results by county: {{legend|#c83737|Paige—60–70%}} {{legend|#d35f5f|Paige—50–60%}} {{legend|#de8787|Paige—40–50%}} {{legend|#87cdde|Tynio—40–50%}} ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = H. Brooke Paige, who also won the Republican nominations for [[United States Senate election in Vermont, 2018|U.S. Senate]], state [[Vermont Attorney General|Attorney General]], state [[Secretary of State of Vermont|Secretary of State]], state [[Vermont State Treasurer|Treasurer]] and state [[Vermont Auditor of Accounts|Auditor]], withdrew from all but the Secretary of State race on August 24 in order to allow the Vermont Republican Party to name replacement candidates.{{cite web|url=https://vtdigger.org/2018/08/24/republicans-clock-paige-withdraws-five-statewide-races/|title=Republicans on the clock after Paige withdraws from five statewide races|first=Colin|last=Meyn|work=VTDigger|date=August 24, 2018}} The Vermont Republican Party chose Anya Tynio, who came in 2nd place in the primary, to be the Republican nominee.{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Taylor |title=Vt. GOP picks candidates for 5 open slots |url=http://www.wcax.com/content/news/Vt-GOP-Party-picks-candidates-for-five-open-slots-492051131.html |website=WCAX-TV |publisher=Gray Digital Media |accessdate=30 August 2018}} ==Progressive primary== ===Candidates=== ====Write-in==== * Daniel Freilich, candidate for [[United States Senate election in Vermont, 2010|U.S. Senate in 2010]], Navy medical doctor, physician at the VA Medical Center (also running in Democratic primary) ===Debates & forums=== * [https://youtube.com/watch?v=FQQBSiM85Hw BCTV Meet The Candidates forum for Representative to US House 7/10/2018] ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Progressive primary resultshttps://vtelectionresults.sec.state.vt.us/Index.html#/federal }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Peter Welch (write-in) | party = Vermont Progressive Party | votes = 237 | percentage = 36.9 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate= Daniel Freilich (write-in) | party= Vermont Progressive Party | votes = 73 | percentage = 11.4 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate= Other write-in | party= Vermont Progressive Party | votes = 72 | percentage = 11.2 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Spoiled votes | party = Vermont Progressive Party | votes = 1 | percentage = 0.2 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Blank votes | party = Vermont Progressive Party | votes = 260 | percentage = 40.4 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 643 | percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box end}} ==Liberty Union/Socialist nomination== The [[Liberty Union Party]] serves as the Vermont affiliate of the [[Socialist Party USA|Socialist Party]] for federal-level elections. ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Laura S. Potterhttps://www.sec.state.vt.us/media/914034/2018-general-election-candidate-listing.xlsx ====Withdrawn==== * Ben Mitchell, [[Liberty Union Party|Liberty Union]] nominee for [[Governor of Vermont]] in [[Vermont gubernatorial election, 2010|2010]] and for [[Lieutenant Governor of Vermont]] in [[Vermont elections, 2012#Lieutenant Governor|2012]] (also ran in Democratic primary before dropping out)https://votesmart.org/candidate/51155/benjamin-mitchell#.W2LnadIzqUm ====Declined==== * Erica Clawson, nominee for Representative to U.S. House in [[United States House of Representatives election in Vermont, 2016|2016]] ==United States Marijuana nomination== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Cris Ericson, perennial candidate{{cite web|title=Cris Ericson U.S. Marijuana Party – Vermont|url=https://crisericson.com/|}} ==America First nomination== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Paul Young{{cite web|title=Interview with The America First Party|url=https://thirdpartyinformation.tumblr.com/post/169449309806/interview-with-the-america-first-party|}} (failed to appear on ballot) ==General election== ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" |- valign=bottom !
